memo.headline: Put next quarter's effort on usability: it carries the largest complaint load, and its top named issue, ads interrupting free listeners, is a defined, fixable problem
situation: All reviews in the run were classified. Of the labelled reviews, complaints and praise are the two largest intents, so the negative signal is substantial but not overwhelming.

The top-ranked issue, other.general_negative, scores {C4} from {C1} complaints at a mean severity of {C3}. It is a catch-all for post-update disappointment and has no single fixable component, so it is a poor target for a focused team.

The second-ranked issue, billing.premium_only_controls, scores {C8} from {C5} complaints at a mean severity of {C7}. Customers object to song selection, skipping and next-track controls requiring Premium.
The third-ranked issue, usability.ads_interruptions, scores {C12} from {C9} complaints at a mean severity of {C11}.
Playback and access issues are less frequent but more severe per complaint: playback.stops_skips_glitches has a mean severity of {C15} and access.login_failure has {C19}.

top_issues.why_it_matters: It tops the ranking at {C4} priority from {C1} complaints, driven by customers saying a recent update removed basic features. It is diffuse and low in per-complaint severity ({C3}), so it needs breaking down into specific features before it can be assigned to a team.

Second-ranked at {C8} priority from {C5} complaints with mean severity {C7}. Customers describe basic controls as locked behind Premium after an update. It is largely a monetisation and policy choice rather than a defect.

Third-ranked at {C12} priority from {C9} complaints at mean severity {C11}. Reviewers cite ads after every song or two and say they do not want to be pushed into Premium. It is the main issue inside the usability area, which has the largest complaint load of the four focus areas.
Fourth-ranked at {C16} priority from {C13} complaints, but with a high mean severity of {C15}. Reviewers report music stopping mid-song, not resuming, and voice-assistant playback failing.
Fifth-ranked at {C20} priority from {C17} complaints, with the highest mean severity of the named issues at {C19}. Affected customers cannot reach their account at all.

recommendation.argument: Usability has the largest share of complaints of any focus area, ahead of billing_support, playback and access. Its named issue, usability.ads_interruptions, ranks third at {C12} priority from {C9} complaints. Unlike the first-ranked other.general_negative, which is too diffuse to assign, ad load and interruption frequency are concrete product behaviours a team can measure and tune. Reviewers say the ad frequency itself pushes them away, for example 'every 1 or 2 song then instant ads', and some report uninstalling. Work here should start with ad cadence for free users and extend to the update-related feature complaints that overlap with the diffuse top issue.

alternatives.case_for: billing.premium_only_controls ranks second at {C8} priority from {C5} complaints, and billing and support combined carry the second-largest complaint load among the four areas.
alternatives.why_not_now: The complaints are about which controls sit behind Premium, which is a pricing and packaging decision rather than a defect. A product team cannot fix it without a commercial policy change, and the data gives no evidence on revenue impact.

alternatives.case_for: playback.stops_skips_glitches has a high mean severity of {C15}, so the complaints that exist are serious, and the failures are real bugs with clear fixes.
alternatives.why_not_now: The issue has far fewer complaints ({C13}) and a lower priority score ({C16}) than the top three issues, so fixing it addresses a smaller share of dissatisfaction.

alternatives.case_for: access.login_failure has the highest mean severity ({C19}) among the named issues, and a customer who cannot log in cannot use the product at all.
alternatives.why_not_now: Only {C17} complaints put it fifth by priority score ({C20}), and access has the smallest complaint load of the four areas. It is better handled as a targeted bug fix than as a quarter-long focus.

limitations: Reviews are self-selected public text, so they over-represent frustrated and highly motivated users and cannot be read as the full customer base.
Severity scores come from automated classification, and a meaningful fraction of records were flagged as needing review, so individual labels may be wrong.
The data does not support claims about churn, revenue or user counts, and complaint counts are not adjusted for how many users each issue affects.
other.general_negative is a catch-all category, so its rank reflects grouped dissatisfaction rather than one identifiable problem.
The evidence pack is a small set of verbatim quotes per issue and may not represent every complaint in that issue.
